key_terms.الْمَشِيئَةُ: al-mashi'ah: the Will or Volition of God; a key term in Islamic theology (kalam) distinguishing God's active will from His eternal essence
key_terms.مُحْدَثَةٌ: muhdathah: originated, brought into being, non-eternal; the theological term for that which had a beginning in time

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the nature of God's Will — is it eternal or created?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared in this brief but profound theological statement that the Divine Will (al-mashi'ah) is 'originated' (muhdathah) — meaning it is not co-eternal with God but is itself a created reality. This was a central position in early Shia kalam (speculative theology), distinguishing the Will from God's eternal essence. The context of this chapter — which deals with whether the Will is an attribute of the act (sifat al-fi'l) rather than an attribute of the essence (sifat al-dhat) — places this hadith within the broader Shia theological framework that safeguards Divine transcendence.
